data.long_meaning: A woman of fragrant perfume, one who brings sweetness and beauty to the world. data.cultural_impact: The name Khusnia is believed to have originated from the Arabic language. In Arabic, "Khusr" means "despair" or "sorrow" and "Al-Khunnas" means "fragrant" or "sweet-smelling." Together, the name Khusnia can be interpreted as a woman with a sweet fragrance or one who brings sweetness and beauty to the world. In various Islamic cultures, perfume is a symbol of beauty, purity, and a connection to the divine. Thus, the name Khusnia is a reminder of the power of beauty, positivity, and sweetness in life.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic spirituality, the name Khusania holds great significance. As mentioned earlier, the name embodies the essence of sweet fragrance and positivity. According to Islamic tradition, every human being has a spirit (Ruh) and a soul (Nafs). The soul is considered the essence of a person and the spirit is the societal and ethical aspect. The Islamic belief emphasizes the importance of the spirit and the soul living in harmony to lead a virtuous and fulfilling life. The name Khusnia can serve as a reminder of the importance of maintaining a sweet fragrance in life, both internally and externally. This can be achieved through acts of kindness, good character, and leading a virtuous life, which in turn, can bring pleasure to oneself and those around them. By carrying this name, an individual may be inspired to strive towards living a life that spreads positivity and sweetness, just like the fragrance of perfume.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Fragrant, Perfume" symbolizes A woman of fragrant perfume, one who brings sweetness and beauty to the world. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Khusnia serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of fragrant, perfume.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Khusnia bint Abdul-Muttalib was the wife of the Prophet Muhammad. The name Khusnia carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: She was a member of the Banu Hashim clan and is believed to have been one of the wives of the Islamic prophet Muhammad.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Khusnia remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.
